title: API Gateway (HTTP versus REST versus WebSocket)
hook: Amazon API Gateway fronts your APIs with throttling, authentication, and integration to Lambda, HTTP backends, or AWS services. HTTP APIs are cheaper and faster for most REST use cases; REST APIs offer older feature depth; WebSocket APIs maintain persistent bidirectional connections.

blocks.text: HTTP API (v2) is the default choice for Lambda and HTTP proxy integrations — lower cost and latency. REST API (v1) supports API keys, request validation, AWS WAF, usage plans, and more integration types — needed when those features matter. WebSocket API manages connect, message, and disconnect routes for real-time apps. All three terminate TLS at the edge and integrate with Amazon Cognito or Lambda authorizers.

entries.plainDefinition: Lightweight API Gateway flavor for common REST and Lambda patterns.
Full-featured API Gateway with usage plans, API keys, and request validators.
Backend target — Lambda, HTTP URL, mock, AWS service.
entries.example: HTTP proxy to internal ALB URL.

blocks.text: API Gateway is the serverless edge — pay per request, built-in throttling, no EC2 to patch. Choosing HTTP vs REST affects cost and features. WebSocket vs Socket.io on ALB is a common comparison. Interviewers ask about Lambda proxy integration, authorizers, and when to put CloudFront in front.

blocks.title: Default pick
blocks.body: Start HTTP API unless you need REST-only features: usage plans, request validation, or certain legacy integration types.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — HTTP API to Lambda
snippet.code:
HttpApi:
  Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api
  Properties:
    Name: orders-api
    ProtocolType: HTTP

Integration:
  Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Integration
  Properties:
    ApiId: !Ref HttpApi
    IntegrationType: AWS_PROXY
    IntegrationUri: !GetAtt OrderFunction.Arn
    PayloadFormatVersion: "2.0"

Route:
  Type: AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Route
  Properties:
    ApiId: !Ref HttpApi
    RouteKey: POST /orders
    Target: !Sub integrations/${Integration}
snippet.explanation: HTTP API uses ApiGatewayV2 resources with simpler model than REST v1.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — REST API usage plan
snippet.code:
UsagePlan:
  Type: AWS::ApiGateway::UsagePlan
  Properties:
    UsagePlanName: partner-tier
    Throttle:
      RateLimit: 100
      BurstLimit: 200
    ApiStages:
      - ApiId: !Ref RestApi
        Stage: prod
snippet.explanation: Usage plans and API keys are REST API v1 features — not on HTTP API.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: REST API for simple Lambda when HTTP API suffices — higher cost. HTTP API when you need usage plans/API keys. 29-second Lambda timeout with 30s API Gateway max for non-async. Missing CORS on HTTP API routes.

blocks.text: HTTP API supports JWT authorizers natively; REST supports more mapping templates and caching (deprecated patterns). Private integrations reach VPC Link to NLB/ALB inside VPC. How to prove it in production: API Gateway execution logs; 429 from throttling; X-Ray traces from API Gateway to Lambda; compare p99 HTTP API vs REST for same Lambda.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Cost and latency for Lambda BFF
Connection state in DynamoDB often needed

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying HTTP and REST APIs are the same. Strong answer: HTTP API v2 for most serverless REST; REST v1 when usage plans/API keys/validators required; WebSocket for persistent connections.

interviewTakeaways: HTTP API (v2): default for Lambda/HTTP — lower cost and latency.
REST API (v1): usage plans, API keys, request validation, broader legacy integrations.
WebSocket API: $connect/$disconnect routes for bidirectional real-time.
60s: HTTP for most REST. REST when usage plans/API keys needed. WebSocket for live connections. VPC Link for private ALB/NLB backends.
Follow-up: how does VPC Link differ from public HTTP integration?
commonPitfalls: Choosing REST API for every project — rejected when HTTP API meets requirements at lower cost.
Strong answer: match API type to feature needs; HTTP API is default in 2024+ greenfield.
Lambda in VPC without NAT/endpoints — API Gateway invokes OK but Lambda cannot reach RDS.
WebSocket API without DynamoDB for connection IDs — broadcast fails across instances.

jsTsCorrelations.note: API Gateway HTTP API v2 event differs from REST v1 — Node handlers checking event.requestContext.http.path must match deployed API type.
API Gateway v2 types from @types/aws-lambda differ from v1 APIGatewayProxyEvent — TypeScript projects break when migrating HTTP to REST or vice versa.
